scope: Managed-service-first Phase Zero architecture and dogfood package.

sources.note: Canonical private repository and clean develop baseline.
Private RULE-034/DEC-035 provenance at pinned commit.

findings: The existing modular-monolith foundation can host declarative Phase Zero without runtime changes.
Project intake supports Agency, client, third-party, and direct-discovery origins with a mandatory internal readiness gate.
The realistic repository-first scenario preserves cost and reversibility while exposing machine-checkable invariants.
No MCP, provider, cloud resource, persistence, API, UI, deployment, merge, or financial action is activated.
contrary_evidence: Declarative consistency does not prove future runtime authorization, isolation, retrieval safety, or customer value.
The separate wiki cannot be synchronized safely while it contains unrelated local changes.
Identity, project isolation details, retention, UI topology, and Agency transport remain open before their implementation triggers.
assumptions: Repository-driven dogfooding is sufficient for the internal Phase Zero.
Candidate bounded contexts will be validated by Event Storming before persistence.
divergences: The previous subscription-first wording was superseded for MVP priority while subscription self-service remains a later modality.

cost.note: Internal execution/review time only; no fixed hours or commercial price approved.

recommendation: Freeze a core commit for read-only independent review; keep completion blocked until findings are resolved and the exact final commit passes review.
